correctness.rationale: For n>=3 the exhaustive feasible/infeasible closure distinction is correct: incompatible edges force E; a matching leaving >=4 uncovered vertices forces no new edge; one leaving exactly 2 forces one completion; a perfect matching is closed. This yields exactly two families of inclusion-minimal nonclosed premises. Each must be an antecedent in any complete implication basis because all proper subsets are closed; the constructed basis computes closure in one synchronous round. Matching counts establish the rank polynomial and the Möbius recurrence gives all intervals, including top -He_{2m}(1). The explicit poset map has principal lower preimages with greatest elements and meets the published simple-homotopy fiber theorem. Independent brute-force incidence intersection checks cover all 32768 edge subsets of K6, all predicted closed subsets and 15000 additional K8 inputs; Möbius recurrence was checked in 138 K6 and 2502 K8 intervals. The proof, not extrapolation, establishes general n.

Their known tools are cited and are insufficient alone to imply the explicit nonbipartite one-factor lattice and sharp globally minimal direct rule count without the new closure and minimal-premise analysis. The prior bipartite permutation-incidence result is a different graph family and has different Laguerre/chessboard invariants. Searches did not show exact prior coverage; priority remains contingent on an independent literature review.

value.rationale: Positive one-factor edge contexts are canonical finite knowledge representations; an exact globally optimal one-pass basis is a nontrivial resource invariant, while the lattice rank sizes, Hermite Möbius polynomial, and simple-homotopy transfer supply distinct algebraic and topological invariants. Unlike the bipartite permutation analogue, this one-factor family is nonbipartite and links to the different topology of complete-graph matching complexes, for which considerable current research exists. The known matching-complex types and generic poset theorem are credited; the claim is the motivated, self-contained context-specific synthesis rather than a raw table or an arbitrary instance.
